<translate>
<!--T:1-->
<code>general-server.json</code> controls the server-wide and world-wide behavior of DragonMineZ: progression and Training Points, world generation, the story, racial skills, world bosses, player data storage and more. It matters for dedicated servers, LAN worlds and singleplayer saves alike, whenever you want tighter control over how a world plays.
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:2-->
The file lives at <code>config/dragonminez/general-server.json</code>. The server sends it to every client that joins (and again after <code>/dmzreload config</code>), so clients always use the server's values. This page explains every setting in the file, what each value does, and the ranges DMZ enforces when it reads them.
</translate>

{{Note|type=config|title=<translate><!--T:3--> Combat lives in its own file</translate>|text=<translate><!--T:4--> Stamina, blocking and parrying, damage mitigation, combat flight and ki weapon tuning are not part of this file. They live in <code>config/dragonminez/combat.json</code>, documented on [[Special:MyLanguage/Combat Config|Combat Config]].</translate>}}

<translate>
== Comments in the file == <!--T:5-->
</translate>
{{See also|How to JSON}}
<translate>
<!--T:6-->
The file DMZ generates is plain JSON without comments. DMZ's parser tolerates <code>//</code> comments and ignores keys that start with <code>_</code>, <code>$</code> or <code>//</code>, but every time DMZ rewrites the file (a version upgrade, <code>/dmzconfig</code>, the in-game config editor) those comments and notes are removed. Keep your notes outside the file.
</translate>

<translate>
== File overview == <!--T:7-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:8-->
The file is split into these top-level sections:
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:9--> Section</translate> !! <translate><!--T:10--> Purpose</translate>
|-
| <code>configVersion</code> || <translate><!--T:11--> Version stamp used for config upgrades. Do not hand-edit it.</translate>
|-
| <code>worldGen</code> || <translate><!--T:12--> Structures, Dragon Ball generation, the Otherworld toggle and structure distances.</translate>
|-
| <code>gameplay</code> || <translate><!--T:13--> Progression, TP gain and cost, story and side-quest toggles, the Otherworld revive, food recovery, relic items, fusion, parties, difficulty multipliers and capsules.</translate>
|-
| <code>racialSkills</code> || <translate><!--T:14--> Enables and tunes each race's racial skill (one sub-object per race).</translate>
|-
| <code>dynamicGrowth</code> || <translate><!--T:15--> Practice-based stat growth, documented on [[Special:MyLanguage/Dynamic Growth|Dynamic Growth]].</translate>
|-
| <code>gravity</code> || <translate><!--T:16--> Gravity per dimension, gravity training and the Gravity Device, documented on [[Special:MyLanguage/Gravity Config|Gravity Config]].</translate>
|-
| <code>mutant</code> || <translate><!--T:17--> The Mutant lottery and its rage meter.</translate>
|-
| <code>falseSuperSaiyan</code> || <translate><!--T:18--> The hidden False Super Saiyan form for Saiyans.</translate>
|-
| <code>kiTransfer</code> || <translate><!--T:19--> Ki Transfer between players: rate, bonus, penalty, ranges and timings.</translate>
|-
| <code>superSaiyanGodRitual</code> || <translate><!--T:20--> The Super Saiyan God Ritual: participants, circle, timings, power, duration and cooldowns.</translate>
|-
| <code>worldBoss</code> || <translate><!--T:21--> World boss contribution, knockouts, revives and rewards.</translate>
|-
| <code>crafting</code> || <translate><!--T:22--> What Dr. Kikono's Station copies from the template item.</translate>
|-
| <code>storage</code> || <translate><!--T:23--> The player data storage backend (NBT, JSON or database).</translate>
|-
| <code>developer</code> || <translate><!--T:24--> The in-chat JSON problem report.</translate>
|-
| <code>hair</code> || <translate><!--T:25--> Limits for the hair editor.</translate>
|}

<div id="configVersion"></div>
<translate>
== Config version == <!--T:26-->
</translate>
{{See also|How to JSON}}
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:27--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:28--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:29--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>configVersion</code> || <translate><!--T:30--> A semantic version string, for example <code>"2.2.0"</code></translate> || <translate><!--T:31--> Do not change it. DMZ compares it with the mod's config version to decide whether the file must be upgraded.</translate>
|}

<div id="worldGen"></div>
<translate>
== World generation == <!--T:32-->
</translate>
{{See also|Structures|Dragons and Wishes|Otherworld}}
<translate>
<!--T:33-->
The <code>worldGen</code> block controls DMZ structures, Dragon Balls and the Otherworld.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:34--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:35--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:36--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>generateCustomStructures</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:37--> Enables DMZ structures in world generation.</translate>
|-
| <code>generateDragonBalls</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:38--> Enables Dragon Ball generation and re-scattering after a wish.</translate>
|-
| <code>otherworldActive</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:39--> Keeps the Otherworld gameplay systems active. If <code>false</code>, the Otherworld isn't used and vanilla respawn applies instead.</translate>
|-
| <code>dbSpawnRange</code> || <code>1000</code> || <translate><!--T:40--> Spawn radius of the built-in Earth and Namek Dragon Balls around world spawn. Clamped to <code>100</code>–<code>6000</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>dragonBallSets</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate><!--T:41--> How many copies of each built-in Earth and Namek Dragon Ball are scattered (<code>1</code>–<code>10</code>; <code>0</code> counts as <code>1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>structureMinDistanceFromSpawn</code> || <code>500</code> || <translate><!--T:42--> Minimum distance DMZ structures spawn from the world origin (always at least 16 blocks below the maximum).</translate>
|-
| <code>structureMaxDistanceFromSpawn</code> || <code>10000</code> || <translate><!--T:43--> Maximum distance DMZ structures spawn from the world origin (enforced minimum of <code>3000</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>structureMinDistanceBetween</code> || <code>500</code> || <translate><!--T:44--> Minimum distance kept between individual DMZ structures.</translate>
|-
| <code>structureSpacing</code> || <code>6000</code> || <translate><!--T:45--> Spacing in blocks (minimum <code>256</code>) for structure sets that use the <code>dragonminez:wide_random_spread</code> placement type. None of DMZ's built-in structures use it; it is there for datapacks.</translate>
|-
| <code>structureSeparation</code> || <code>2000</code> || <translate><!--T:46--> Minimum separation in blocks for the same placement type (always below the spacing).</translate>
|}

<div id="gameplay"></div>
<translate>
== Gameplay == <!--T:47-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:48-->
The <code>gameplay</code> block is the largest section of the file: progression, TP, the story, the Otherworld, food, relics, fusion, parties and difficulty tuning.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Core progression === <!--T:49-->
</translate>
{{See also|Stats and Attributes|Transformations|Custom Forms}}
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:50--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:51--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:52--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>forceCharacterCreation</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:53--> Forces new players through character creation on their first login.</translate>
|-
| <code>commandOutputOnConsole</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:54--> Also logs DMZ command output to the server console.</translate>
|-
| <code>maxLevelValueInsteadOfStats</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:55--> <code>true</code>: <code>maxValue</code> is the '''level''' cap, and stat points can be spread freely as long as the total stays under <code>maxValue × 6</code>. <code>false</code>: each individual stat is also capped at <code>maxValue</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>maxValue</code> || <code>1000000</code> || <translate><!--T:56--> The cap read together with <code>maxLevelValueInsteadOfStats</code> (minimum <code>1000</code>). The total of all six stats can never exceed <code>maxValue × 6</code>, and the player level runs from 1 to <code>maxValue</code> across that range.</translate>
|-
| <code>vitCurveKnee</code> || <code>16000.0</code> || <translate><!--T:57--> VIT value at which health per VIT point reaches the class <code>VIT_scaling_max</code>. Below it, the per-point scaling rises quadratically from the class minimum; above it, it stays at the maximum.</translate>
|-
| <code>defCurveKnee</code> || <code>20000.0</code> || <translate><!--T:58--> The same curve for DEF (<code>DEF_scaling_max</code>), used for flat damage mitigation.</translate>
|-
| <code>levelFormRequisiteEnabled</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:59--> Enforces the minimum player level a form can require.</translate>
|-
| <code>sagaFormRequisiteEnabled</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:60--> Enforces the saga quest a form can require before it unlocks. Ignored when <code>storyModeEnabled</code> is <code>false</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>multiplicationInsteadOfAdditionForMultipliers</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:61--> <code>false</code>: form, stack form and effect multipliers stack additively (easier to balance). <code>true</code>: they multiply each other (weaker at low values, synergy-heavy at high progression).</translate>
|-
| <code>ultimateFormFixedValue</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:62--> <code>false</code>: the Ultimate stack form adds its bonus on top of the best base form the player owns. <code>true</code>: Ultimate only uses the multiplier written in its own form file.</translate>
|}

<translate>
=== TP gain === <!--T:63-->
</translate>
{{See also|Training Points and Mastery|Hyperbolic Time Chamber|Effects}}
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:64--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:65--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:66--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>tpGainMultiplier</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:67--> Global TP multiplier (the <code>GLOBAL</code> boost below).</translate>
|-
| <code>increaseTPGainRelativeToTPCost</code> || <code>0.75</code> || <translate><!--T:68--> Extra TP gain that grows as stat costs rise: <code>1 + value × √(current stat cost / stat cost at progressionReferenceLevel)</code>, capped at <code>1 + value</code>. <code>0</code> disables it. Applies to every TP source except training minigames (<code>TRAINING</code>). Not applied when manual TP purchases are disabled in [[Special:MyLanguage/Dynamic Growth|Dynamic Growth]].</translate>
|-
| <code>progressionReferenceLevel</code> || <code>10000</code> || <translate><!--T:69--> Player level whose stat cost gives the full <code>increaseTPGainRelativeToTPCost</code> bonus (minimum <code>2</code>, never above <code>maxValue</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>attributeRewardPointRatio</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:70--> Share of an '''Attributes''' reward (quests, Power Boost wishes, world bosses) given as Attribute Points, rounded down; the rest is given as the TP those stat points cost the player at that moment. Clamped to <code>0</code>–<code>1</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>tpHealthRatio</code> || <code>0.25</code> || <translate><!--T:71--> TP earned from a kill, scaled by the target's max health.</translate>
|-
| <code>tpPerHit</code> || <code>2</code> || <translate><!--T:72--> Flat TP per successful hit.</translate>
|-
| <code>passiveTpGain</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate><!--T:73--> Flat TP gained passively over time.</translate>
|-
| <code>tpPer20BlocksTraveled</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate><!--T:74--> TP gained per 20 blocks traveled.</translate>
|-
| <code>tpPerBlockMined</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate><!--T:75--> TP gained per block mined.</translate>
|-
| <code>tpPerItemCrafted</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate><!--T:76--> TP gained per item crafted.</translate>
|-
| <code>gravityBonusEnabled</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:77--> Enables the gravity TP bonus (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Gravity Config|Gravity Config]]).</translate>
|-
| <code>HTCTpMultiplier</code> || <code>1.75</code> || <translate><!--T:78--> TP multiplier inside the Hyperbolic Time Chamber (minimum <code>1.0</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>otherworldDeadTpMultiplier</code> || <code>2.0</code> || <translate><!--T:79--> TP multiplier for dead players inside the Otherworld (minimum <code>1.0</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>storyResetTPMultiplier</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:80--> Story quest TP rewards after a story reset wish: run 1 gives 100%, run 2 gives 50%, run 3 gives 25%, and so on. Clamped to <code>0</code>–<code>1</code>; <code>1.0</code> disables the decay.</translate>
|-
| <code>kamiBlessTpMultiplier</code> || <code>1.2</code> || <translate><!--T:81--> TP multiplier while under Kami's Blessing (minimum <code>1.0</code>). Counts as a <code>POTION</code> boost.</translate>
|-
| <code>kamiBlessDurationSeconds</code> || <code>300</code> || <translate><!--T:82--> Duration of Kami's Blessing, which Dende gives to players with good alignment.</translate>
|-
| <code>kamiBlessCooldownSeconds</code> || <code>1800</code> || <translate><!--T:83--> Cooldown before Dende can bless the same player again.</translate>
|}

<translate>
=== TP cost formula === <!--T:84-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:85-->
The TP cost of the next stat point is calculated like this:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
TotalStats = STR + SKP + RES + VIT + PWR + ENE
StatCap    = maxValue × 6
Knee       = StatCap × 0.05
Multiplier = globalTPCostMultiplier × race tpCost multiplier

Variable   = TotalStats × 1.25                                                    (TotalStats ≤ Knee)
           = Knee × 1.25 + (Knee × 1.25 / 0.7) × ((TotalStats / Knee)^0.7 − 1)   (above the knee)
BaseCost   = minTPCost + Variable
Discount   = maxTPDiscount − TotalStats      (only while TotalStats < maxTPDiscount)

FinalCost  = max(minTPCost, BaseCost × Multiplier − Discount)
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
<!--T:86-->
If <code>dynamicGrowth.attributeTpCostMultiplier</code> is above <code>1.0</code>, the final cost is multiplied by it (rounded up). When <code>dynamicGrowth.manualTpPurchasesEnabled</code> is <code>false</code>, stats can't be bought with TP at all. Stat points earned through [[Special:MyLanguage/Dynamic Growth|Dynamic Growth]] are left out of <code>TotalStats</code> unless <code>dynamicGrowth.growthStatsCountForTpCost</code> is <code>true</code>.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:87--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:88--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:89--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>globalTPCostMultiplier</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:90--> Global multiplier on stat TP costs (minimum <code>0.01</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>minTPCost</code> || <code>16</code> || <translate><!--T:91--> Base and minimum TP cost of one stat point.</translate>
|-
| <code>maxTPDiscount</code> || <code>140</code> || <translate><!--T:92--> Early-game TP discount threshold; the discount fades out as total stats rise.</translate>
|}

<div id="tpGainBoosts"></div>
<translate>
=== TP gain boosts === <!--T:93-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:94-->
<code>tpGainBoosts</code> controls which multiplier ''sources'' apply to each TP-gain ''source''. Its keys are TP sources (<code>STORY</code>, <code>PASSIVE</code>, <code>TRAVEL</code>, <code>MINED</code>, <code>CRAFTED</code>, <code>KILL</code>, <code>HIT</code>, <code>TRAINING</code>); its values are lists of boosts. DMZ writes them in upper case; lower-case names are accepted too.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:95--> Boost</translate> !! <translate><!--T:96--> Multiplier it applies</translate>
|-
| <code>CLASS</code> || <translate><!--T:97--> The player class TP multiplier.</translate>
|-
| <code>RACIALSKILL</code> || <translate><!--T:98--> The Frost Demon racial TP boost (<code>racialSkills.frostdemon.tpBoost</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>HTC</code> || <translate><!--T:99--> <code>HTCTpMultiplier</code> inside the Hyperbolic Time Chamber.</translate>
|-
| <code>OTHERWORLD</code> || <translate><!--T:100--> <code>otherworldDeadTpMultiplier</code> for dead players in the Otherworld.</translate>
|-
| <code>GRAVITY</code> || <translate><!--T:101--> The gravity training bonus (only if <code>gravityBonusEnabled</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>WEIGHTS</code> || <translate><!--T:102--> The weighted equipment bonus.</translate>
|-
| <code>GLOBAL</code> || <translate><!--T:103--> <code>tpGainMultiplier</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>POTION</code> || <translate><!--T:104--> TP effects, including Kami's Blessing.</translate>
|-
| <code>MUTANT</code> || <translate><!--T:105--> <code>mutant.tpGainMultiplier</code> for Mutant players.</translate>
|-
| <code>DIFFICULTY</code> || <translate><!--T:106--> The Easy or Hard TP multiplier of the player's story difficulty.</translate>
|}

<translate>
<!--T:107-->
The generated default gives every source every boost except <code>DIFFICULTY</code>, which only applies to <code>STORY</code> (quest rewards):
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
"tpGainBoosts": {
  "STORY":    ["CLASS", "RACIALSKILL", "HTC", "OTHERWORLD", "GRAVITY", "WEIGHTS", "GLOBAL", "POTION", "MUTANT", "DIFFICULTY"],
  "PASSIVE":  ["CLASS", "RACIALSKILL", "HTC", "OTHERWORLD", "GRAVITY", "WEIGHTS", "GLOBAL", "POTION", "MUTANT"],
  "TRAVEL":   ["CLASS", "RACIALSKILL", "HTC", "OTHERWORLD", "GRAVITY", "WEIGHTS", "GLOBAL", "POTION", "MUTANT"],
  "MINED":    ["CLASS", "RACIALSKILL", "HTC", "OTHERWORLD", "GRAVITY", "WEIGHTS", "GLOBAL", "POTION", "MUTANT"],
  "CRAFTED":  ["CLASS", "RACIALSKILL", "HTC", "OTHERWORLD", "GRAVITY", "WEIGHTS", "GLOBAL", "POTION", "MUTANT"],
  "KILL":     ["CLASS", "RACIALSKILL", "HTC", "OTHERWORLD", "GRAVITY", "WEIGHTS", "GLOBAL", "POTION", "MUTANT"],
  "HIT":      ["CLASS", "RACIALSKILL", "HTC", "OTHERWORLD", "GRAVITY", "WEIGHTS", "GLOBAL", "POTION", "MUTANT"],
  "TRAINING": ["CLASS", "RACIALSKILL", "HTC", "OTHERWORLD", "GRAVITY", "WEIGHTS", "GLOBAL", "POTION", "MUTANT"]
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
<!--T:108-->
Boosts stack additively: <code>1 + Σ(boost − 1)</code>, plus the <code>increaseTPGainRelativeToTPCost</code> bonus, which applies to every source except <code>TRAINING</code>. Each TP gain is boosted once.
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:109-->
<code>STORY</code> covers TP that doesn't come from one of the other sources: <code>TPS</code> quest rewards, raid and tournament rewards, TP wishes and similar lump sums. The TP half of an <code>ATTRIBUTES</code> reward or wish is computed from the player's stat cost and is never boosted.
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:110-->
Remove a boost from a source's list to stop that multiplier from applying to it (for example, remove <code>GRAVITY</code> from <code>MINED</code> if you don't want mining TP boosted by gravity training). A source that is present with an empty list (<code>"MINED": []</code>) gets no boosts at all; a source missing from the map uses its default list.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Story and side quests === <!--T:111-->
</translate>
{{See also|Sagas|Custom Quests|Reloading and Updating Changes}}
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:112--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:113--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:114--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>storyModeEnabled</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:115--> Master toggle for sagas.</translate>
|-
| <code>createDefaultSagas</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:116--> Generates DMZ's default sagas and saga quests in the world save if they're missing (needs <code>storyModeEnabled</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>sideQuestsEnabled</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:117--> Master toggle for side quests.</translate>
|-
| <code>createDefaultSideQuests</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:118--> Generates DMZ's default side quests if they're missing.</translate>
|-
| <code>autoUpdateQuests</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:119--> Upgrades DMZ's default quest, saga and side-quest files in the world save when a new DMZ version changes them, keeping your edits. <code>false</code>: default files are only written when they are missing.</translate>
|-
| <code>defaultQuestPartyMultiplier</code> || <code>1.45</code> || <translate><!--T:120--> Party-size difficulty multiplier for quest objectives (clamped to <code>1.0</code>–<code>5.0</code>).</translate>
|}

<translate>
=== Otherworld and Baba's revive === <!--T:121-->
</translate>
{{See also|Otherworld|Fortuneteller Baba}}
<translate>
<!--T:122-->
With the Otherworld active, a dead player is sent to the Otherworld. [[Special:MyLanguage/Fortuneteller Baba|Fortuneteller Baba]] can send them back to the living world for a limited time (a temporary revive); [[Special:MyLanguage/King Yemma|King Yemma]] teleports them back when they are alive or temporarily revived.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:123--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:124--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:125--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>reviveCooldownSeconds</code> || <code>180</code> || <translate><!--T:126--> Time after death before Baba can revive the player.</translate>
|-
| <code>babaTemporaryRevive</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:127--> <code>true</code>: Baba grants a timed return; the player keeps the halo and walks the living world until the timer runs out. <code>false</code>: Baba fully revives the player.</translate>
|-
| <code>babaTempReturnSeconds</code> || <code>3600</code> || <translate><!--T:128--> Length of a temporary return (minimum <code>1</code>). The timer pauses in the Otherworld and while knocked out, and each new temporary return drains faster (up to 5×). Lethal hits during a temporary return knock the player out and cut the timer instead of killing them.</translate>
|-
| <code>babaTimeMultiplierPerWorld</code> || <translate><!--T:129--> See below</translate> || <translate><!--T:130--> A map of dimension id to number: how fast the temporary-return timer drains in each dimension. Active forms also drain it faster.</translate>
|-
| <code>defaultBabaTimeMultiplier</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:131--> Drain speed for dimensions not listed in <code>babaTimeMultiplierPerWorld</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>babaHardcoreEnabled</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:132--> If <code>true</code>, each death makes the next revive cooldown longer.</translate>
|-
| <code>babaHardcoreCooldownGrowth</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:133--> With hardcore on, the cooldown is <code>reviveCooldownSeconds × (1 + growth × (deaths − 1))</code>.</translate>
|}

<translate>
<!--T:134-->
Default <code>babaTimeMultiplierPerWorld</code>:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
"babaTimeMultiplierPerWorld": {
  "minecraft:overworld": 1.0,
  "minecraft:the_nether": 2.0,
  "minecraft:the_end": 3.0,
  "dragonminez:namek": 1.0,
  "dragonminez:time_chamber": 5.0,
  "dragonminez:sacredkaiplanet": 1.0
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
=== Senzu Beans === <!--T:135-->
</translate>
{{See also|Senzu Bean}}
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:136--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:137--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:138--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>senzuCooldownTicks</code> || <code>240</code> || <translate><!--T:139--> Cooldown between Senzu Bean uses (also used by the Medi-Bug ant).</translate>
|-

|}

<div id="food"></div>
<translate>
=== Food restoration === <!--T:142-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:143-->
With the <code>food</code> block, any food item's normal hunger and saturation restoration also restores a proportional slice of health, ki and stamina. Default value:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
"food": {
  "minHungerPoints": 2,
  "maxHungerPoints": 20,
  "minSaturationPoints": 0.4,
  "maxSaturationPoints": 2.0,
  "healthPercentageRecoveredPerHungerPoint": 0.01,
  "kiPercentageRecoveredPerHungerPoint": 0.01,
  "staminaPercentageRecoveredPerHungerPoint": 0.02,
  "healthPercentageRecoveredPerSaturationPoint": 0.001,
  "kiPercentageRecoveredPerSaturationPoint": 0.001,
  "staminaPercentageRecoveredPerSaturationPoint": 0.004,
  "blacklistedNamespaces": [],
  "blacklistedItems": []
}
</syntaxhighlight>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:144--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:145--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:146--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>minHungerPoints</code> / <code>maxHungerPoints</code> || <code>2</code> / <code>20</code> || <translate><!--T:147--> Food that restores fewer hunger points than the minimum gives no hunger-based recovery; anything above the maximum counts as the maximum.</translate>
|-
| <code>minSaturationPoints</code> / <code>maxSaturationPoints</code> || <code>0.4</code> / <code>2.0</code> || <translate><!--T:148--> The same rule for the food's saturation modifier.</translate>
|-
| <code>healthPercentageRecoveredPerHungerPoint</code> || <code>0.01</code> || <translate><!--T:149--> Fraction of max health restored per hunger point.</translate>
|-
| <code>kiPercentageRecoveredPerHungerPoint</code> || <code>0.01</code> || <translate><!--T:150--> Fraction of max ki restored per hunger point.</translate>
|-
| <code>staminaPercentageRecoveredPerHungerPoint</code> || <code>0.02</code> || <translate><!--T:151--> Fraction of max stamina restored per hunger point.</translate>
|-
| <code>healthPercentageRecoveredPerSaturationPoint</code> || <code>0.001</code> || <translate><!--T:152--> Fraction of max health restored per saturation point.</translate>
|-
| <code>kiPercentageRecoveredPerSaturationPoint</code> || <code>0.001</code> || <translate><!--T:153--> Fraction of max ki restored per saturation point.</translate>
|-
| <code>staminaPercentageRecoveredPerSaturationPoint</code> || <code>0.004</code> || <translate><!--T:154--> Fraction of max stamina restored per saturation point.</translate>
|-
| <code>blacklistedNamespaces</code> || <code>[]</code> || <translate><!--T:155--> List of mod namespaces (for example <code>"farmersdelight"</code>) whose food is excluded from this recovery.</translate>
|-
| <code>blacklistedItems</code> || <code>[]</code> || <translate><!--T:156--> List of specific item ids (for example <code>"minecraft:golden_apple"</code>) excluded from this recovery.</translate>
|}

|-
| <code>sacredWaterMultiplier</code> || <code>1.1</code> || <translate><!--T:164--> Permanent all-stats multiplier from drinking Sacred Water (once per character). Clamped to <code>1.0</code>–<code>100.0</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>demonEyeMultiplier</code> || <code>1.5</code> || <translate><!--T:165--> All-stats multiplier while wearing the Demon Eye. Clamped to <code>1.0</code>–<code>100.0</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>demonEyeKiDrainPercent</code> || <code>0.02</code> || <translate><!--T:166--> Fraction of max ki drained per second while the Demon Eye is worn.</translate>
|-
| <code>demonEyeHealthDrainPercent</code> || <code>0.02</code> || <translate><!--T:167--> Fraction of max health drained per second once ki runs out (never below 1 health).</translate>
|-
| <code>demonEyeAlignmentLossIntervalSeconds</code> || <code>10</code> || <translate><!--T:168--> Every this many seconds the wearer loses 1 alignment. <code>0</code> disables it.</translate>
|-
| <code>demonEyeMaxGrowth</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:169--> How much the wearer grows in size (<code>0.5</code> means up to 50% bigger).</translate>

|-
| <code>demonEyeBackHitsToRemove</code> || <code>3</code> || <translate><!--T:171--> Melee hits from behind that knock the Demon Eye off. <code>0</code> disables it.</translate>
|-
| <code>demonEyeBackHitWindowSeconds</code> || <code>10</code> || <translate><!--T:172--> Time window in which those hits must land.</translate>
|}

<div id="capsules"></div>
<translate>
=== Capsules === <!--T:181-->
</translate>
{{See also|Capsules}}
<translate>
<!--T:182-->
Stat capsule items grant stat points to the stat or stats configured in the <code>capsules</code> block:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
"capsules": {
  "statSeparator": ", ",
  "values": {
    "<CAPSULE_TYPE>": { "stats": "STR, PWR", "points": 5 }
  }
}
</syntaxhighlight>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:183--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:184--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:185--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>statSeparator</code> || <code>", "</code> || <translate><!--T:186--> Separator used when a capsule lists several stats.</translate>
|-
| <code>values</code> || <translate><!--T:187--> One entry per capsule type</translate> || <translate><!--T:188--> A map of capsule type to <code>{ stats, points }</code>: which stat or stats each capsule type boosts, and how many points it grants (default <code>5</code>).</translate>
|}

<translate>
=== Party === <!--T:189-->
</translate>

! <translate><!--T:190--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:191--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:192--> What it does</translate>

|-
| <code>partyMaxLevelGap</code> || <code>500</code> || <translate><!--T:194--> Maximum level difference allowed between party members (<code>-1</code> means unlimited).</translate>
|-
| <code>partyTpShareRatio</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:195--> Fraction of TP shared with party members (clamped to <code>0</code>–<code>10</code>). Members only receive it in the same dimension and within the earner's Instant Transmission range.</translate>
|-
| <code>enemyHealthPerPartyPlayer</code> || <code>1.25</code> || <translate><!--T:196--> Enemy health multiplier per additional party member.</translate>
|-
| <code>enemyDamagePerPartyPlayer</code> || <code>1.1</code> || <translate><!--T:197--> Enemy damage multiplier per additional party member.</translate>
|-
| <code>partyMarkerRange</code> || <code>2000</code> || <translate><!--T:198--> Maximum distance (in blocks, same dimension) at which party members' on-screen markers are shown.</translate>
|}

</translate>

</translate>

<div id="racialSkills"></div>
<translate>
== Racial skills == <!--T:223-->
</translate>
{{Main|Racial Skills}}
<translate>
<!--T:224-->
The <code>racialSkills</code> block enables and tunes each race's racial skill. Each race has its own sub-object. Files from older versions that still use the old flat keys (<code>saiyanZenkaiAmount</code>, <code>majinAbsoprtionSkill</code>, …) are converted to this layout automatically when the file is upgraded.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:225--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:226--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:227--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>enableRacialSkills</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:228--> Global on/off switch for every racial skill.</translate>
|}

<translate>
<!--T:229-->
Ratios in the tables below are fractions (<code>0.25</code> means 25%).
</translate>

<div id="glind"></div>
<translate>
=== Glind === <!--T:348-->
</translate>
{{See also|Glind|Alignment}}
<translate>
<!--T:349-->
Sub-object <code>glind</code>.
</translate>

<div id="dynamicGrowth"></div>
<translate>
== Dynamic growth == <!--T:367-->
</translate>
{{Main|Dynamic Growth}}
<translate>
<!--T:368-->
The <code>dynamicGrowth</code> block configures practice-based stat growth. It has more than 20 fields and its own anti-farming logic, so it is documented on its own page.
</translate>

<div id="gravity"></div>
<translate>
== Gravity == <!--T:369-->
</translate>
{{Main|Gravity Config}}
<translate>
<!--T:370-->
The <code>gravity</code> block configures dimension gravity, the [[Special:MyLanguage/Gravity Device|Gravity Device]] and weight-based training zones. With more than 60 fields, it is documented on its own page.
</translate>

<div id="mutant"></div>
<translate>
== Mutant == <!--T:371-->
</translate>
{{See also|Effects|Transformations}}
<translate>
<!--T:372-->
The <code>mutant</code> block controls a periodic server-wide lottery: every interval, a handful of players are rolled for a chance to become a [[Special:MyLanguage/Mutant|Mutant]]. Mutants get TP and mastery multipliers and a rage meter that lets them use the forms of the <code>legendaryGroupName</code> group, even without owning them, while the meter is full or active.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:373--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:374--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:375--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>enabled</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:376--> Master toggle.</translate>
|-
| <code>rollIntervalMinutes</code> || <code>30</code> || <translate><!--T:377--> Minutes between lottery rolls (minimum <code>1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>playersPerRoll</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate><!--T:378--> Players considered per roll.</translate>
|-
| <code>chance</code> || <code>0.20</code> || <translate><!--T:379--> Chance (<code>0</code>–<code>1</code>) that a considered player becomes a Mutant.</translate>
|-
| <code>maxHolders</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate><!--T:380--> Maximum concurrent Mutant holders server-wide.</translate>
|-
| <code>legendaryGroupName</code> || <code>"legendaryforms"</code> || <translate><!--T:381--> The form group the rage meter gives access to (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Custom Forms|Custom Forms]]).</translate>
|-
| <code>tpGainMultiplier</code> || <code>1.25</code> || <translate><!--T:382--> TP multiplier while Mutant (the <code>MUTANT</code> boost).</translate>
|-
| <code>masteryGainMultiplier</code> || <code>1.50</code> || <translate><!--T:383--> Form mastery gain multiplier while Mutant.</translate>
|-
| <code>rageBorrowedFormBonus</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:384--> A legendary form the Mutant doesn't own (borrowed through the rage meter) is worth the player's best unlocked non-legendary form (with its mastery) plus this much on each stat bonus (scaled per stat like the legendary form), capped at the legendary form at full mastery. Minimum <code>0</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>powerBonusBoostWithSkill</code> || <code>0.33</code> || <translate><!--T:385--> An owned legendary form gets its bonus raised by this fraction while rage is active.</translate>
|-
| <code>keepMutantOnDeath</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:386--> If <code>false</code>, dying removes Mutant status.</translate>
|-
| <code>rage</code> || <translate><!--T:387--> See below</translate> || <translate><!--T:388--> Rage meter tuning (an object).</translate>

<translate>
=== Rage meter === <!--T:389-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:390-->
The <code>mutant.rage</code> object tunes the rage meter. The meter fills from damage dealt to worthy targets and damage taken. A full meter while in a legendary-group form starts the active phase, which drains it; when it empties, a borrowed form is reverted. Out of combat it drains on its own. Death resets it.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:391--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:392--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:393--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>gainPerDealtHealthFraction</code> || <code>60.0</code> || <translate><!--T:394--> Rage gained per full health bar of damage dealt (proportional to the fraction removed).</translate>
|-
| <code>gainPerReceivedHealthFraction</code> || <code>150.0</code> || <translate><!--T:395--> Rage gained per full health bar of damage taken.</translate>
|-
| <code>maxGainPerHit</code> || <code>25.0</code> || <translate><!--T:396--> Maximum rage from a single hit.</translate>
|-
| <code>significantTargetHealthRatio</code> || <code>0.10</code> || <translate><!--T:397--> Damage dealt only counts against players or mobs whose max health is at least this fraction of the attacker's.</translate>
|-
| <code>significantDamageTakenRatio</code> || <code>0.01</code> || <translate><!--T:398--> Damage taken only counts when it is at least this fraction of max health.</translate>
|-
| <code>varietyBonusPerStep</code> || <code>0.25</code> || <translate><!--T:399--> Extra gain for each change of attack type (melee, strike, ki).</translate>
|-
| <code>varietyMaxSteps</code> || <code>4</code> || <translate><!--T:400--> Maximum variety steps.</translate>
|-
| <code>varietyWindowSeconds</code> || <code>4.0</code> || <translate><!--T:401--> Time window for an attack-type change to count.</translate>
|-
| <code>activeDurationSeconds</code> || <code>10.0</code> || <translate><!--T:402--> How long a full meter lasts once active.</translate>
|-
| <code>activeGainMultiplier</code> || <code>0.35</code> || <translate><!--T:403--> Gain multiplier while active.</translate>
|-
| <code>fullIdleSeconds</code> || <code>15.0</code> || <translate><!--T:404--> Out-of-combat time before a full meter starts draining.</translate>
|-
| <code>partialIdleSeconds</code> || <code>8.0</code> || <translate><!--T:405--> Out-of-combat time before a partial meter starts draining.</translate>
|-
| <code>idleDrainSeconds</code> || <code>3.0</code> || <translate><!--T:406--> Time for an idle meter to drain completely.</translate>
|}

<div id="falseSuperSaiyan"></div>
<translate>
== False Super Saiyan == <!--T:407-->
</translate>
{{See also|Saiyan}}
<translate>
<!--T:408-->
The <code>falseSuperSaiyan</code> block controls a hidden Saiyan form that can't be bought or selected: it is granted by a rage meter that charges while a Saiyan without Super Saiyan is badly hurt, and it ends when the meter empties. Mutants never get it (the Mutant rage meter takes priority).
</translate>

<div id="kiTransfer"></div>
<translate>
== Ki Transfer == <!--T:429-->
</translate>
{{See also|Ki Transfer}}
<translate>
<!--T:430-->
The <code>kiTransfer</code> block controls [[Special:MyLanguage/Ki Transfer|Ki Transfer]]: holding {{Key|Ctrl}} + {{Key|Alt}} + {{Key|Right Mouse}} on another player sends them a share of your Ki and boosts their STR, SKP, DEF and PWR, while the giver is slowed, locked out of combat and weakened by Ki Exhaustion. The link is also how the Super Saiyan God Ritual gathers its givers. Negative or invalid numbers fall back to the default.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:431--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:432--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:433--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>enabled</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:434--> Master toggle. Turning it off also ends every active link.</translate>
|-
| <code>kiPercentPerSecond</code> || <code>0.025</code> || <translate><!--T:435--> Fraction of the giver's max Ki sent every second (at most <code>1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>boostDelaySeconds</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:436--> How long a giver must hold the link before boosting the receiver and counting as a giver for the Super Saiyan God Ritual.</translate>
|-
| <code>boostPerDonor</code> || <code>0.05</code> || <translate><!--T:437--> STR, SKP, DEF and PWR bonus per giver, applied on top of the receiver's other multipliers.</translate>
|-
| <code>maxBoostDonors</code> || <code>5</code> || <translate><!--T:438--> Maximum number of givers that count for the bonus (minimum <code>0</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>donorSpeedMultiplier</code> || <code>0.4</code> || <translate><!--T:439--> Walking and flying speed multiplier while giving (<code>0</code>–<code>1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>interruptDamageRatio</code> || <code>0.10</code> || <translate><!--T:440--> The link breaks once the giver has taken damage adding up to this fraction of their max health since it started (minimum <code>0.01</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>startRange</code> || <code>8.0</code> || <translate><!--T:441--> Range in blocks to start a link (minimum <code>1</code>). The server allows 2 extra blocks for movement and needs line of sight.</translate>
|-
| <code>maxLinkDistance</code> || <code>32.0</code> || <translate><!--T:442--> The link breaks when the players are farther apart than this (never less than <code>startRange</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>attackChargeCreditRatio</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:443--> Ki that overflows the receiver's bar while they charge a ki attack is stored for that attack, up to this fraction of the receiver's max Ki.</translate>

| <code>intervalSeconds</code> || <code>3.0</code> || <translate><!--T:444--> Length of a transfer interval. Each completed interval adds a stack of Ki Exhaustion to the giver and lingering time to both players.</translate>

|-

<div id="superSaiyanGodRitual"></div>
<translate>
== Super Saiyan God Ritual == <!--T:449-->
</translate>
{{See also|Super Saiyan God Ritual|Saiyan}}
<translate>
<!--T:450-->
The <code>superSaiyanGodRitual</code> block controls the [[Special:MyLanguage/Super Saiyan God Ritual|Super Saiyan God Ritual]]: when enough pure-hearted Saiyans in the right forms give their Ki to another Saiyan with Ki Transfer, they gather into a ring and channel, and the receiver rises and turns into a hidden form that lasts a limited time. The form itself (colors, aura, drain) is defined in the Saiyan form group named by <code>groupName</code>, whose <code>formType</code> must stay <code>godritual</code> (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Custom Forms|Custom Forms]]). Negative or invalid numbers fall back to the default.
</translate>

! <translate><!--T:451--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:452--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:453--> What it does</translate>

<div id="worldBoss"></div>
<translate>
== World bosses == <!--T:477-->
</translate>
{{Main|World Bosses}}
<translate>
<!--T:478-->
The <code>worldBoss</code> block tunes the world boss fights. Contribution points are the four totals (damage dealt, damage mitigated, damage received, healing) multiplied by their weights. Healing counts more when the healed player's defense and blocking soak a lot of damage (up to 10 times).

<!--T:479-->
World boss health and damage aren't keys of this block: they follow the Hard difficulty multipliers. Each boss has its saga fight's Normal health × <code>hardModeHPMultiplier</code> × 4 and its Normal damage × <code>hardModeDamageMultiplier</code> (both in the difficulty multipliers of the <code>gameplay</code> section above). The values on the [[Special:MyLanguage/World Bosses|World Bosses]] pages use the defaults.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:480--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:481--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:482--> What it does</translate>

|-
| <code>audienceRefreshSeconds</code> || <code>5</code> || <translate><!--T:484--> How often the participant list, and with it the boss's group scaling, is refreshed.</translate>
|-
| <code>meterLingerSeconds</code> || <code>15</code> || <translate><!--T:485--> How long the contribution HUD stays on screen after the kill.</translate>
|-
| <code>damageWeight</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:486--> Weight of damage dealt to the boss and its minions.</translate>
|-
| <code>mitigatedWeight</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:487--> Weight of damage mitigated (defense, blocks, barriers).</translate>
|-
| <code>receivedWeight</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:488--> Weight of damage received.</translate>
|-
| <code>healedWeight</code> || <code>1.0</code> || <translate><!--T:489--> Weight of healing done.</translate>
|-

|-

|-

|-
| <code>reviveInterruptCooldownSeconds</code> || <code>15</code> || <translate><!--T:494--> Revive cooldown after the cast is interrupted.</translate>
|-
| <code>reviveInterruptDamageRatio</code> || <code>0.10</code> || <translate><!--T:495--> A revive cast is interrupted once the caster has taken damage adding up to this fraction of their max health (minimum <code>0.01</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>reviveDecayMultiplier</code> || <code>3.0</code> || <translate><!--T:496--> While nobody is reviving a downed player, their revive progress drains this many times faster than one caster fills it (minimum <code>1</code>, rounded to a whole number).</translate>
|-
| <code>truceGraceSeconds</code> || <code>15</code> || <translate><!--T:497--> After a fight ends, the players who took part in it can't hurt each other for this many seconds.</translate>
|-
| <code>reviveRange</code> || <code>6.0</code> || <translate><!--T:498--> Range to start a revive.</translate>
|-
| <code>reviveRestoreRatio</code> || <code>0.25</code> || <translate><!--T:499--> Health, ki and stamina restored by a revive.</translate>
|-
| <code>knockoutTitleSeconds</code> || <code>5</code> || <translate><!--T:500--> Duration of the knockout title.</translate>
|-
| <code>rankChanceBonus</code> || <code>[0.25, 0.15, 0.10]</code> || <translate><!--T:501--> List of drop chance bonuses for the 1st, 2nd and 3rd best contributors.</translate>
|-
| <code>guaranteedRewardMinRatio</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:502--> Guaranteed rewards (<code>chance</code> 1.0) scale from this fraction up to 100% with the player's points compared to the best player.</translate>
|-
| <code>minContributionShare</code> || <code>0.075</code> || <translate><!--T:503--> Minimum share of total points needed to receive any reward (<code>0.075</code> = 7.5%). Players below it get nothing.</translate>
|-
| <code>healthPerExtraMember</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:504--> Extra boss max health for each participant after the first, as a fraction of its health: with <code>0.5</code>, 2 fighters give ×1.5 and 4 give ×2.5. Participants in Creative or Spectator mode don't count. <code>0</code> turns it off.</translate>
|-
| <code>damagePerExtraMember</code> || <code>0.25</code> || <translate><!--T:505--> The same for the boss's melee and ki damage.</translate>
|-
| <code>rewards</code> || <translate><!--T:506--> See below</translate> || <translate><!--T:507--> A map of boss key to reward list: the rewards of each boss.</translate>
|}

<translate>
=== Boss rewards === <!--T:508-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:509-->
Each reward entry uses the same fields as a quest reward (<code>type</code>, <code>item</code>/<code>count</code>, <code>amount</code>, <code>skill</code>/<code>level</code>, <code>command</code>, <code>formGroup</code>/<code>formName</code>, …) plus <code>chance</code> (<code>0</code>–<code>1</code>, default <code>1.0</code>). The built-in rewards pay <code>ATTRIBUTES</code> (Janemba 500, Turles 50, Metal Cooler Core 105, Tamagami Number 3, 2 and 1 90, 300 and 360, Gomah 435) instead of TP. A boss missing from the map uses its built-in rewards; write <code>"&lt;boss key&gt;": []</code> to disable drops for one boss.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:510--> Boss key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:511--> World boss</translate>
|-
| <code>janemba</code> || {{L|Janemba}}
|-
| <code>turles</code> || {{L|Turles}}
|-
| <code>metal_cooler_core</code> || {{L|Metal Cooler Core}}
|-
| <code>tamagami_3</code> || {{L|Tamagami Number 3}}
|-
| <code>tamagami_2</code> || {{L|Tamagami Number 2}}
|-
| <code>tamagami_1</code> || {{L|Tamagami Number 1}}
|-
| <code>gomah</code> || {{L|Gomah}}
|}

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
"rewards": {
  "janemba": [
    { "type": "ATTRIBUTES", "amount": 500, "chance": 1.0 },
    { "type": "ITEM", "item": "dragonminez:dimensional_sword", "count": 1, "chance": 0.5 },
    { "type": "SKILL", "skill": "dimensional_teleport", "level": 1, "chance": 0.2 }
  ]
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<div id="crafting"></div>
<translate>
== Crafting == <!--T:512-->
</translate>
{{See also|Armor}}
<translate>
<!--T:513-->
The <code>crafting</code> block decides what Dr. Kikono's Station copies from the template item into the crafted result.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:514--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:515--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:516--> What it copies</translate>
|-
| <code>copyEnchantmentsFromTemplate</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:517--> Enchantments.</translate>
|-
| <code>copyWeaponLevelFromTemplate</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:518--> Weapon level (Weapon Leveling compatibility).</translate>
|-
| <code>copyWeaponLevelProgressFromTemplate</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:519--> Weapon level progress (Weapon Leveling compatibility).</translate>
|-
| <code>copyApotheosisRarityFromTemplate</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:520--> Apotheosis rarity.</translate>
|-
| <code>copyApotheosisAffixesFromTemplate</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:521--> Apotheosis affixes.</translate>
|-
| <code>copyApotheosisSocketsFromTemplate</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:522--> Apotheosis sockets.</translate>
|-
| <code>copyApotheosisGemsFromTemplate</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:523--> Apotheosis gems (only when sockets are copied too).</translate>
|}

<div id="storage"></div>
<translate>
== Storage == <!--T:524-->
</translate>
{{See also|Notice to Server Owners}}
<translate>
<!--T:525-->
The <code>storage</code> block chooses where player data is saved. Case matters for <code>storageType</code>.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:526--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:527--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:528--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>storageType</code> || <code>"NBT"</code> || <translate><!--T:529--> <code>NBT</code>, <code>JSON</code> or <code>DATABASE</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>host</code> || <code>"localhost"</code> || <translate><!--T:530--> Database host (<code>DATABASE</code> only).</translate>
|-
| <code>port</code> || <code>3306</code> || <translate><!--T:531--> Database port (<code>DATABASE</code> only).</translate>
|-
| <code>database</code> || <code>"dragonminez"</code> || <translate><!--T:532--> Database name.</translate>
|-
| <code>table</code> || <code>"player_data"</code> || <translate><!--T:533--> Table name.</translate>
|-
| <code>username</code> || <code>"root"</code> || <translate><!--T:534--> Database user.</translate>
|-
| <code>password</code> || <code>"password"</code> || <translate><!--T:535--> Database password. Change it in production.</translate>
|-
| <code>poolSize</code> || <code>10</code> || <translate><!--T:536--> Database connection pool size (minimum <code>1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>threadPoolSize</code> || <code>4</code> || <translate><!--T:537--> Threads used for asynchronous loads and saves (minimum <code>1</code>).</translate>
|}

<translate>
=== How the backends work === <!--T:538-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:539-->
* <code>NBT</code>: player data only rides on vanilla's own player save (<code>.dat</code>).
* <code>JSON</code>: each player is also saved to <code>&lt;world&gt;/dragonminez/playerdata_json/&lt;uuid&gt;.json</code>.
* <code>DATABASE</code>: each player is also saved to a MariaDB database (<code>jdbc:mariadb</code>), using <code>host</code>, <code>port</code>, <code>database</code>, <code>table</code>, <code>username</code> and <code>password</code>.
* The vanilla <code>.dat</code> save is '''always''' written. With <code>JSON</code> or <code>DATABASE</code>, the extra store is loaded on login and overrides the vanilla values; it is saved on logout and every 5 minutes.
</translate>

{{Note|type=warning|title=<translate><!--T:540--> If the database fails</translate>|text=<translate><!--T:541--> If the database connection fails, DMZ does '''not''' switch to another backend: it logs the error and player data is only kept in the vanilla <code>.dat</code> save. Check the server log if data doesn't seem to persist.</translate>}}

{{Note|type=danger|title=<translate><!--T:542--> Switching backends</translate>|text=<translate><!--T:543--> Don't switch <code>storageType</code> on a server with players online. Do it with the server empty, and take a backup first.</translate>}}

<div id="developer"></div>
<translate>
== Developer == <!--T:544-->
</translate>
{{See also|How to JSON}}
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:545--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:546--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:547--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>reportJsonProblemsInChat</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:548--> On login, shows every player a summary of the JSON files that failed to load (configs, quests, wishes, Dragon Ball packs) and of the default files that were auto-upgraded. The server log has the full details.</translate>
|}

<div id="hair"></div>
<translate>
== Hair == <!--T:549-->
</translate>
{{See also|Character Customization}}
<translate>
<!--T:550-->
The <code>hair</code> block sets the limits of the hair editor. The server trims any hair style that exceeds them.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:551--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:552--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:553--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>maxSegmentsPerStrand</code> || <code>12</code> || <translate><!--T:554--> Maximum segments per strand (clamped to <code>1</code>–<code>32</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>maxStrandLength</code> || <translate><!--T:555--> <code>20.0</code> for <code>base</code>, <code>ssj</code>, <code>ssj2</code>, <code>ssj3</code> and <code>ssj4</code></translate> || <translate><!--T:556--> A map of hair slot to number: the maximum strand length per hair slot (clamped to <code>0.5</code>–<code>128</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>maxStrandWidth</code> || <code>8.0</code> || <translate><!--T:557--> Maximum strand width (clamped to <code>0.25</code>–<code>16</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>maxRootOffset</code> || <code>2.0</code> || <translate><!--T:558--> Maximum offset of a strand root (clamped to <code>0</code>–<code>4</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>maxTotalSegmentsPerStyle</code> || <code>600</code> || <translate><!--T:559--> Maximum segments in a whole hair style (clamped to <code>1</code>–<code>2176</code>).</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Reload and validate == <!--T:560-->
</translate>
{{See also|Reloading and Updating Changes|How to JSON}}
<translate>
<!--T:561-->
# Edit <code>config/dragonminez/general-server.json</code>.
# Validate the JSON syntax.
# Run <code>/dmzreload config</code> (or <code>/dmzreload</code>). Single values can also be changed live with <code>/dmzconfig general-server &lt;section&gt; &lt;key&gt; &lt;value&gt;</code>.
# If the file has a syntax error, DMZ keeps running on the default values, leaves your file untouched and reports the file, line and column in the log (and in chat on login, see the developer section above). Fix it and reload again.
</translate>

{{Navbox Configuration}}
